question: On 16 June 2025, the Commission replied to parliamentary question E-001083/20251 signed by multiple Members concerning the safety and transparency regarding the health risks posed by menstrual products due to the documented presence of hazardous substances in these products. In its reply, the Commission mentions in particular that a REACH restriction on skin sensitisers is currently in preparation.

France and Sweden notified their intention to submit a restriction proposal on skin sensitisers on 11 January 2018 and submitted it on 12 April 2019. The combined opinion of the Committee for Risk Assesment (RAC) and the Committee for Socio-economic Analysis (SEAC) was adopted on 17 September 2020, almost six years ago.

That opinion supported France and Sweden’s proposal to restrict the use of skin sensitising substances in clothing, footwear and other items with similar skin contact, with expected health benefits equivalent to at least EUR 708 million per year. 1.
Since the opinion of the European Chemicals Agency (ECHA) was adopted, what concrete actions has the Commission taken to act on this restriction proposal?
What is the expected timeline for the Commission to come forward with a draft proposal for a restriction on skin sensitisers?
How does the Commission factor the cost of inaction into its preparatory work, in particular considering the six years of additional exposure since the adoption of the ECHA opinion?
answer: EN on behalf of the European Commission (8.9.2026) The Commission is fully committed to protecting the environment and human health when implementing the Regulation on the Registration, Evaluation, Authorisation and Restriction of Chemicals (REACH)1.

The Commission began its work on the restriction on skin-sensitising substances in clothing, footwear and other articles that come into contact with human skin shortly after receipt of the proposal from the European Chemicals Agency (ECHA)2.

The Commission notes the complexity of this file, given its broad scope (covering more than 1 000 substances) and the resulting challenge of developing a restriction proposal that is both proportionate to the identified risk and operational.

The Commission has engaged with Member States’ competent authorities (including enforcement authorities), industry, non-governmental organisations and laboratories, with the objective of finding practical solutions to different challenges related to future compliance, enforcement and recycling.

The Commission is aware of the health benefits of the proposed restriction and remains fully committed to proposing a restriction that is effective and enforceable in practice, and workable for both authorities and economic operators. The Commission intends to present a draft restriction to the REACH Committee as soon as possible.
1 Regulation (EC) No 1907/2006 of the European Parliament and of the Council of 18 December 2006

concerning the Registration, Evaluation, Authorisation and Restriction of Chemicals (REACH), establishing a European Chemicals Agency, amending Directive 1999/45/EC and repealing Council Regulation (EEC) No 793/93 and Commission Regulation (EC) No 1488/94 as well as Council Directive 76/769/EEC and Commission Directives 91/155/EEC, 93/67/EEC, 93/105/EC and 2000/21/EC, https://eur-lex.europa.eu/eli/reg/2006/1907/oj.
